record.original_question: Construct a hierarchy of higher helicity-type invariants for divergence-free vector fields so that when all lower invariants vanish, the first nonzero invariant gives a lower bound for the field's energy.

evidence.quote: Problem 34 ([6]). Find a sequence of higher helicity invariants for vector fields so that, given a field, if all the previous invariants are equal to zero for it, then the first nonzero invariant bounds the field’s energy from below. We refer to the book [6] and its second edition for the discussion of open problems and a large bibliography on the subject, see also [46, 30, 81, 108].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian 3-manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $\mathcal{V}(M)$ denote the space of smooth divergence-free vector fields on $M$ that are tangent to the boundary. For $v \in \mathcal{V}(M)$, define its energy by
$$E(v) = \int_M \|v(x)\|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}(x),$$
and its helicity by
$$\mathcal{H}(v) = \int_M \langle v, \operatorname{curl}^{-1} v \rangle \, d\mathrm{vol},$$
where $\operatorname{curl}^{-1} v$ is a vector potential $A$ with $\operatorname{curl} A = v$. Arnold's classical inequality states that there exists a constant $C(M) > 0$ such that $E(v) \geq C(M)\, |\mathcal{H}(v)|$ for all $v \in \mathcal{V}(M)$.

Construct a sequence of functionals $\{I_n : \mathcal{V}(M) \to \mathbb{R}\}_{n \geq 1}$, with $I_1 = \mathcal{H}$, having the following properties:

(i) each $I_n$ is invariant under the action of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ (i.e., is a higher-order helicity-type invariant);

(ii) for every $v \in \mathcal{V}(M)$ and every $n \geq 1$, if $I_1(v) = I_2(v) = \cdots = I_{n-1}(v) = 0$ but $I_n(v) \neq 0$, then there exists a constant $C_n(M) > 0$ (independent of $v$) and an exponent $\alpha_n > 0$ such that
$$E(v) \geq C_n(M)\, |I_n(v)|^{\alpha_n}.$$

In particular, vanishing of all lower invariants forces the first nonzero invariant to bound the energy of the field from below.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, originating in Arnold–Khesin's topological hydrodynamics, remains open in full generality. Partial progress exists: cubic ("third-order") asymptotic helicity-type invariants and certain higher analogs of the asymptotic Hopf invariant have been constructed (e.g., Bodnar/Komendarczyk-Vela-Vick), and a related rigidity result shows helicity is the only regular integral invariant under mild assumptions. However, no general hierarchy giving energy lower bounds when lower invariants vanish has been established.

status_evidence.title: On asymptotic higher analogs of the magnetic helicity invariant in MHD
status_evidence.snippet: Higher invariant of magnetic fields not expressed from asymptotic linking numbers of magnetic lines.
status_evidence.claim: Partial constructions of higher helicity-type invariants exist but do not yield a full hierarchy with energy bounds.

status_evidence.title: Helicity is the only integral invariant of volume-preserving transformations
status_evidence.snippet: Under mild assumptions, helicity is the only integral invariant of volume-preserving transformations.
status_evidence.claim: Rigidity results constrain what higher invariants can look like, indicating the problem remains subtle and open.

status_evidence.title: Dispersion of the Arnold's asymptotic ergodic Hopf invariant
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of higher-order momenta of asymptotic self-linking and cubic magnetic helicities.
status_evidence.claim: Cubic helicity invariants have been introduced, representing partial progress.
